label: input token e at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires when the input is the letter e during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 4 or later. It never fires on e at positions 0-3, on any other token, on <DEL>, or during the copy phase (where e is fed back in as the model output). Magnitude rises steadily with position: about 0.1-0.15 of max at t=4, about 0.44 at t=5, about 0.7 at t=6, and about 0.98 at t=8. Earlier e tokens in the sequence lower it somewhat (first occurrences carry most of the mass). The predicate is near-perfect on dev (P=1.0, R=0.9995). The 20 misses are tiny activations (<0.05) on other tokens at t=8.

issues: The secondary claim that 'an earlier e in the sequence lowers it somewhat' is not supported. On the dev split, repeat e's (in_first=0) average more activation mass per active step (0.186/6836) than first e's (0.814/34856). That comparison is confounded by position, because repeat e's sit later in the sequence. Top examples also show repeat e's at about full strength: 'e y f z z [e:0.49] q t [e:0.99]' and 'n m r 1 e 2 [e:0.72]'. The phrase should be dropped or softened.

'Never fires during the copy phase' is very nearly true but not exact. There are 2 copy-phase activations on dev and a few on test (e.g. step 15 at 0.02 after an earlier e at t=6). All of them are below 0.03 of max, which is scattered noise.

The test-split misses (11 steps, 0.0% of activation mass) are all below 0.02 of max. They sit at t=8 (the last original token of length-9 sequences) or in the copy phase, and they are not a systematic class. There are 0 false positives, so every e at t>=4 in the original phase fires.

The magnitude claims hold: about 0.11-0.14 at t=4, about 0.44 at t=5, about 0.67-0.70 at t=6 and about 0.98-1.0 at t=8. The feature is silent at t=0-3, on <DEL>, and on all other tokens apart from noise. Test split: P=1.0, R=0.9997, F1=0.9999, mass recall 1.0.
